name: Turkopticon
tagline: Worker-led platform organizing mutual aid and advocacy for Amazon Mechanical Turk workers
sdg_alignment: SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth
SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Reliance on Amazon Mechanical Turk platform policies
news_articles: Irani, L. (2015). 'Justice for Data Janitors'. Public Books.
Rosenblat, A., & Stark, L. (2016). 'Uber's Algorithmic Management in the On-Demand Economy'. New Media & Society.
academic_citations: Irani, L., & Silberman, M. S. (2016). Turkopticon: Interrupting worker invisibility in Amazon Mechanical Turk

policy_outcomes.description: Delivered petition to Amazon Mechanical Turk team regarding mass rejections and worker protections

outcome_methodology: Qualitative worker testimonies and documented case studies
documented_limitations: Dependent on Amazon's willingness to implement worker-requested changes
jurisdictional_scope: International, focused on Amazon Mechanical Turk platform
failure_modes: Mass rejections issue remains unresolved after 10+ years of advocacy
curation_criteria: Worker-submitted ratings and reviews of requesters on Amazon Mechanical Turk; community moderation of contributions
